messages:
Maya: Quick sync — PM wants per-org dashboards that show tokens/sec, avg latency (p50/p95), active capacity pools, and a noisy-neighbor signal. We need a telemetry contract from runtime/infra. Who can own schema + ingestion SLAs? cc @Sasha @Jon
Sasha: We can emit most of this, but cardinality explosion is the risk. If we label by tenant+route+model+region+pool we'll kill the TSDB. Need dimensions + cardinality limits.
Jon: Agreed. Proposal: two-tier approach — 1) per-tenant hourly rollups (tokens_total, requests, errors, active_connections) at 1m for top tenants, 5m for the long tail; 2) sampled per-request traces (1000r/s global sample) for latency and kv-cache heatmaps. Traces go to tracing backend, rollups to TSDB.
Maya: PM asked for 1m granularity for SLA dashboards. How realistic is that for all tenants?
Sasha: 1m for all tenants is expensive. We can offer 1m for paid tiers / top-N tenants and aggregated 5m for others. Or support on-demand higher fidelity via opt-in.
Emi: Product requirement: out-of-the-box per-org view in the console. For self-serve customers show summary; for paid customers full panels. Also UX needs to surface sampling and data completeness.
Alex: Security/ops note — must ensure tenant isolation: A cannot query B's raw traces. Need RBAC + per-tenant scoping in the console and enforced row-level security for query engine. Also redact any user-identifying metadata in noisy-neighbor signals.
Jon: Drafting telemetry schema suggestion (feel free to nit):
```
metric: redwood.tokens_total
labels:
  tenant_id: "<tenant id>"
  route: "<route>"
  model: "<model>"
  region: "<region>"
  pool: "<pool_id>"
```
Carrier rules: enforce allowed-values registry and map unknowns to "__other" to cap cardinality.
Sasha: Ingestion contract: runtime must send signed tenant_id header (X-Redwood-Tenant) and a routing key. Ingest pipeline will enrich with org metadata from auth service. Also we need per-tenant ingest quotas so noisy tenants get throttled at ingest time rather than OOMing the TSDB.
Maya: UX/rollout question — how do we indicate partial coverage? PM wants a clear 'confidence' indicator on the dashboard (because we'll be sampling/top-N).
Emi: Recommend: show confidence score + data freshness timestamp + a tooltip that explains sampling/rollup policy. Also an action to request higher fidelity (with billing opt-in).
Alex: Operational plan — implement row-level security in the query layer, only allow console to hit aggregation endpoints (no raw traces unless tenant has opt-in role). Also audit logs for any per-tenant trace access.
Sasha: We'll add a computed metric: redwood.noisy_neighbor_score (0-100) — nightly job that looks at concurrent usage, delta in p95 vs baseline, and error correlation. Publish it as a daily rollup; provide an alert when score > 70.
Jon: Proposed rollout phases: Phase 1 (3w): agree schema, build minimal rollups for top N tenants, console stub with confidence UI. Phase 2 (6w): sampling + traces + RBAC enforcement + noisy_neighbor_score. Phase 3: opt-in higher fidelity + billing. ETA depends on signoff.
Maya: I'll draft a short doc with schema + ingest SLA (latency, retention) + access model. Can owners confirm: Sasha infra owner, Jon runtime owner, Alex SRE owner for RBAC, Emi product owner for UX?
Sasha: +1, will own infra pieces (ingest quotas/registry).
Jon: +1, will own runtime labels and sampling hooks.
Alex: +1 for RBAC and auditing.
Emi: +1 for the UX spec and tooltips.
Maya: Thanks — can we have a quick review in 3 days? I'll post the doc here and mark decisions. @OpsBot set reminder.
OpsBot: Reminder set — review metrics contract in 3 days.
Sasha: quick note — for billing we'll need an endpoint that returns per-tenant token counts with tamperproofing; maybe signed reports or periodic export to billing system.
Jon: For low-latency SLOs the console should fetch pre-aggregated p50/p95 from rollups instead of running ad-hoc queries. That keeps load predictable.
Maya: Good call. I'll include that in the doc. Thanks all. :pray:
Sasha: :+1:
Alex: :eyes:
